h1: A-Star Phulare Valley, Chiang Rai — Valley Pool Villas, a Mountain-View Infinity Pool and a Strawberry Farm
intro: Picture this: you wake up, open your villa door, and find mist drifting over the peaks. You walk over for a soak in an infinity pool whose edge melts into a wall of green mountains, then head down to pick strawberries at the resort's own farm before breakfast — A-Star Phulare Valley, Chiang Rai is a 4-star pool villa resort set among valleys and orchards in Tha Sut, Mueang Chiang Rai district, about 30 min drive north of town · what people talk about most is the mountain-view infinity pool, the Farm to Table strawberry and sheep farm, and the spacious villas starting at 47 sqm · prices start from about THB 3,500/night, with an average review score around 8.8 and Tripadvisor 4.3/5 · but we'll be straight with you — the location is fairly far from town, so we'll lay out both the good and the things to watch.

body.html: The big picture — who A-Star Phulare Valley is for — the shortest summary is this: A-Star Phulare Valley is a resort for people who want to "escape the city" and be fully surrounded by nature, mountains, and quiet · it's not a downtown hotel where you step out onto a walking street or into a coffee shop right away, but a pool villa resort set among valleys and orchards in Tha Sut, about 30 min drive north of Chiang Rai town · the draw is the green valley setting, spacious villas with private balconies, a mountain-view infinity pool, and a strawberry and sheep farm right on the resort grounds · real reviews agree that the people who fit here are couples wanting a quiet, romantic stay, families with small kids who love farm activities, and travelers who have a car or are happy to arrange one rather than tourists who want to stay downtown for a night out · the resort has been open for years and performs consistently well — its average review score on booking platforms sits around 8.8/10, while Tripadvisor gives it 4.3/5 and ranks it #12 of 107 hotels in Chiang Rai, which puts it near the top of the province · if you're after a place where the resort itself is the destination of your trip, not just somewhere to sleep, this is a strong contender — but if you mainly plan to sightsee in town, weigh up the distance first.

Location and getting around — this is both the selling point and the thing to think hard about with A-Star Phulare Valley · the resort sits in Tha Sut, north of Chiang Rai town, ringed by mountains, orchards, and farmland, which gives it a calm atmosphere and fresh air you won't find in the city · the flip side is that it's a fair way out — about a 30-minute drive to the walking street and night bazaar area, and roughly 30 min by car from Chiang Rai's Mae Fah Luang Airport (CEI) too · many foreign reviews say the same thing — "a bit out of the way" — and some even describe it as feeling like you're "in the middle of nowhere," which for some is a plus (the peace and quiet) and for others is a limitation · the upside is that the resort offers a free airport shuttle, and several of Chiang Rai's famous spots are also to the north — Singha Park (Boon Rawd Farm) is not far, and Wat Rong Khun and Wat Rong Suea Ten are within driving range · our honest advice: if you're staying here you should have your own car, rent one, or arrange a private car/taxi in advance, because on-demand ride-hailing in this area isn't as convenient as in town, and the cost of multiple trips in and out of the city can add up to a tidy sum.

"The infinity pool is more beautiful than I can describe — waking up to mist over the mountains, so quiet, genuinely good for relaxing — but you have to drive to get into town, and it's a bit of a hassle without a car."

Room types and decor — A-Star Phulare Valley has around 131 rooms and villas spread across the valley grounds · the entry-level room is the Phuwing at about 47 sqm, which is very generous for a resort's base room, with a private balcony looking out over garden or mountains · from there you move up through higher-grade rooms and villas, all the way to pool villas with a private pool for couples or families who want full privacy · every unit is designed to open onto the surrounding nature, with a balcony or terrace for a morning coffee · on decor, we'll be honest — the style is simple and modern, prioritizing space and views over luxurious materials · some reviews note that certain pieces of furniture and the in-room decor feel a little plain and are starting to show their age, which is worth setting expectations around · that said, what gets consistent praise is the spaciousness of the rooms, balconies with a real view, and overall cleanliness · if views matter to you, we suggest requesting a room or villa facing the valley at the time of booking, since some units see the mountains more clearly than others, and it's the kind of detail that makes a real difference to the experience.

Facilities, pool, and activities — the most talked-about highlight of A-Star Phulare Valley is the infinity pool whose edge blends into the line of mountains · many reviews credit it as the reason they decided to stay, because the pool set against the green valley backdrop really is gorgeous, both on misty mornings and in the warm evening light · around the pool there's a poolside restaurant and bar for a drink with a view · what sets this resort apart is the on-site strawberry and sheep farm, open for guests to wander, feed the sheep, and pick strawberries in season, Farm to Table style — it's an activity families with small kids love, and the main reason many families choose this place · there's also archery, plus bike and ATV rentals for riding around the resort and orchards, a spa for relaxing massages, a fitness room, and large garden grounds for a stroll · the basics like Wi-Fi, parking, and the airport shuttle are free · we'll say it plainly: given how far out the location is, the resort's facilities and activities are the heart of staying here — the more you make of the on-site activities, the more the stay is worth it.

Food and bar — the resort has a poolside restaurant and two bar spots for main meals and evening drinks · what earns the most praise is the breakfast buffet, which is varied and generous; many reviews say the choices are good and the ingredients fresh, some of it grown on the resort's own farm in keeping with the Farm to Table concept · sitting down to breakfast with a morning mountain view is another thing people appreciate · but to be straight, a common observation is that the variety at other meals is fairly limited — because the resort is far from town, heading out to find a restaurant isn't as easy as it is in the city, so most guests end up relying on the resort's dining, and the menu can start to repeat over several nights · our advice: if you're staying for several nights, plan to eat in town sometimes or stop at a restaurant during your day trips to change things up · overall the food is solid for a valley resort, especially breakfast, which is a genuine strong point, but don't expect the range of dining options you'd get at a city hotel.

Service — service is another area that earns consistent praise in real reviews · both on booking platforms and Tripadvisor, people agree that the staff are attentive, friendly, and go out of their way to help guests have a good experience, which goes a long way to offset the location's limitations · many reviews mention the team helping with the shuttle, recommending things to do, and running the farm activities well · for the full picture, though, a few voices say service can be inconsistent at times — for example, water pressure in some villas isn't steady, or there was a case of being charged extra for towels at check-out without prior notice · these observations don't happen to everyone, but it's worth confirming the details of any charges clearly at check-in · overall, service remains a strong point that keeps this place's review scores high.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling from leading booking platforms and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: a beautiful mountain-view infinity pool, a quiet valley setting great for relaxing and romantic trips, spacious villas with private balconies, a strawberry and sheep farm the kids love, a varied and generous breakfast, and friendly, attentive staff · on the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is the location far from town — about a 30-minute drive to the town and airport, which makes it hard for those without a car · next is the limited range of restaurants at the resort, inconsistent water pressure in some villas, decor and furniture that feel plain or are aging in places, and the odd small charge that wasn't flagged in advance · most of these gripes can be fixed or avoided by planning your transport, picking the right villa, and confirming details clearly before you stay, rather than being dealbreakers that keep people from returning.

"Brought the whole family — the kids loved the sheep farm and picking strawberries, and the staff were lovely and took good care of us · the only downside is it's far from town, so we had to eat dinner at the resort every day and the menu started to repeat. Next time we'll rent a car ourselves."

Price and value — entry-level rooms/villas start at around THB 3,500/night in the normal range, climbing to roughly THB 6,000–8,000+ in the cool season (November–January), which is Chiang Rai's high season, as well as on long weekends · pool villas with a private pool sit higher still, depending on size and dates · compared with similar valley resorts or pool villas in Chiang Rai, A-Star Phulare Valley feels good value for room size, views, and on-site activities, especially once you factor in the strawberry farm, sheep farm, infinity pool, and the good breakfast · the value is highest for people who plan to spend several hours a day at the resort and make full use of the activities · but if you plan to head into town to sightsee every day and use the resort just to sleep, the cost of getting in and out and the hassle of hailing a ride can chip away at the value — that crowd may be better suited to a city hotel.

Good to know before you book — a few things help the stay go smoothly · one, transport is the key — if you don't have your own car, rent one, arrange a private car/taxi in advance, or use the resort's free airport shuttle and plan your sightseeing in batches rather than going in and out of town repeatedly · two, if views matter, request a room or villa facing the valley at the time of booking, and choose a pool villa if you want full privacy · three, plan your meals ahead, especially for a multi-night stay — you might alternate eating at the resort with stopping at restaurants on the way to attractions so the menu doesn't repeat · four, the cool season (Nov–Jan) has the best weather and is when the strawberry farm bears fruit, but prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book ahead and compare across platforms · five, confirm the details of any charges and what's included/excluded clearly at check-in to avoid unexpected costs at check-out.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, A-Star Phulare Valley, Chiang Rai is best suited to people who want a quiet valley getaway, in a spacious villa with a mountain view, plus farm activities for the family · the mountain-view infinity pool, the strawberry and sheep farm, the spacious villas from 47 sqm, and the attentive service make the resort itself the destination of the trip, not just a place to sleep · if you're after a downtown stay where you can wander out at night, you don't have your own car, or you want a wide range of restaurants within walking distance, this may not be the answer — consider a hotel in the town area or near the walking street instead · but for a relaxing trip where you want to wake up to mist and mountains, soak in a pool with a view, and let the kids enjoy a farm — A-Star Phulare Valley delivers exactly that kind of stay, memorably, and it's why it has kept high review scores and a top ranking in Chiang Rai for years.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — A-Star Phulare Valley, Chiang Rai

faq.q: Where is A-Star Phulare Valley, and is it easy to get to?
faq.a: It's in Tha Sut, Mueang Chiang Rai district, among valleys and orchards north of the town · it's about a 30-minute drive from both the town and Mae Fah Luang Airport · it's a quiet out-of-town location you can't walk into the city from, so it suits people with a car, a rental, or a pre-arranged private car · the resort offers a free airport shuttle (arrange in advance).

faq.q: How much does A-Star Phulare Valley start at, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 3,500/night for a Phuwing room of around 47 sqm in the normal range · there are higher-grade villas and pool villas with a private pool · prices in the cool season (Nov–Jan) and on long weekends rise fast, so book ahead and compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is A-Star Phulare Valley for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples wanting a quiet, romantic stay and families who enjoy farm activities · you get spacious villas, a mountain-view infinity pool, and an on-site strawberry and sheep farm · if you want a downtown stay for a night out or don't have a car, a hotel in the town area may suit you better.

faq.q: What pool and activities does it have?
faq.a: There's a mountain-view infinity pool as the highlight, and some pool villas have a private pool · on-site activities include a Farm to Table strawberry and sheep farm, archery, bike and ATV rentals, and a spa · there's a poolside restaurant and bar, plus free Wi-Fi and parking.

faq.q: What's the food like at A-Star Phulare Valley?
faq.a: The breakfast buffet earns praise for its variety and quantity, with some of it grown on the resort's own farm · but because it's far from town, the restaurant choice at other meals is fairly limited and the menu may repeat over several nights · for a longer stay, we suggest alternating with meals in town or stops at restaurants on the way to attractions.

faq.q: Is there anything to know or watch out for?
faq.a: Real reviews mention the location far from town at about 30 minutes, limited restaurant choice, inconsistent water pressure in some villas, and decor that feels plain or is aging in places · there have been cases of small charges not flagged in advance at check-out · we suggest planning your transport, picking the right villa, and confirming charges clearly at check-in.
